newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher in moderate volume.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher in moderate volume.

text.p: Israeli bond prices closed higher on Thursday, with most of the activity concentrated in unlinked bonds, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years): +0.11 pct to 168.86
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 pct at 159.73
Volume was moderate at 141 million shekels with CPI-linked bonds recovering for the second straight day, traders said.

"Inflation-linked bonds rose for the second day after sharp losses since Sunday. The yields on long bonds rose from 4.45 percent on Sunday to 4.7 percent on Tuesday and investors realised that they would not rise any further," said Gidi Halperin at Meitav Investments.
"The unlinked bonds continue to post gains on hopes that inflation will decline as the economy is slowing down," said Yoram Ben-Yaeir at Ahrayut Investment Management.
"Demand for the unlinked bonds is also rising despite the fact that yields fell from 15.95 percent on Sunday to 15.8 on Thursday. The unlinked bonds are king of the market," Halperin added.

Makams (which are also unlinked) continued to rise, posting slight gains. Traders noted that yields on the Makams fell from 15.5 percent last week to 15.33 percent. Halperin said that activity in the Makams was falling with total turnover at only 50 million shekels.
"Dollar linked bonds rose on expectations for the dollar's rise," Ben-Yaeir said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
